pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds a NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' column with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that all seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list entries.
The query filters with a bound parameter and ORDER BY id. The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, including id order (ids 3 and 1 set to high).
The unfiltered query uses ORDER BY id. The 'AC-4' test checks the full list.
nav() renders all four filters, with the current one in <strong>. The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
The code returns 400 for any present value outside the Set. The 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks that no <li> appears.

Commit 8eb4520 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) edited this acceptance item after the go. It added 'verified by review: checked by hand', and the spec records no owner decision for the change. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step, so the item is unmet by the rules. The 'AC-7' test does exist and the code behaves correctly. The edit also split the sentence, which now reads '...(or normal, low); — verified by review...'.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test checks it. The route-check script and its shell test were updated to accept a query.

findings.what: Commit 8eb4520 changed AC-7 after the go. It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand'. The spec has no dated owner decision recording this, and the step is not a real, followable step. It also garbles the sentence, leaving a stray ';' before the dash.
findings.fix: Revert the edit to AC-7. The 'AC-7' test already proves the item. If the owner really wants a review step, record a dated decision and give a concrete step (a URL and what it shows).

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but commit 8eb4520 edited an acceptance item in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit, or disclose it in the PR body with the owner's decision.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec intent. The only addition beyond the ask is the traffic route-check relaxation, which the PR discloses and AC-8 needs.
All four state-table rows have tests. AC-7 was edited after the go in the late commit and is flagged.

Tests are behavioural and each is named by its AC. The states are covered. I did not run the tests; CI runs them on every push. The traffic test's fake app was extended without loosening any assertion.
The README documents the filter. It is adequate.
The code is correct. The priority value is validated and bound as a parameter. Extra COUNT query only runs on an empty filtered result.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the priority value is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter, and the nav is built from constants. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond a plain server-rendered HTML string; no browser review was possible.
There is no browser session or UI flow to demonstrate.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because of commit 8eb4520.
